transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you. Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble at work lately. 

Whenever I have to do real, sitting-down brain work... like the monthly reports, or planning out multi-site health events... it feels like I just hit a wall. I keep putting it off, even when I know it matters. So... yeah. That's mainly why I'm here.
Did you have trouble focusing like this when you were a child?

Yeah... I guess so. Um. Even back in elementary school, it was kind of like that. My teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but... that I was always daydreaming. I lost worksheets a lot. I'd usually forget to turn in my homework unless my mom went through my backpack every night to check. So... yeah.
Do you have this same kind of trouble focusing and following through outside of work too?

Yeah... I guess. I mean, I'm still getting by, at work and... you know, out in the community. But... things slip. Deadlines. Sometimes people end up having to cover the gaps for me. It's... well, it's embarrassing. I've had to make a lot of last-minute apologies to coworkers... and to friends, too. So... yeah. It happens outside of work.
Do you spend a lot of your time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

No... not really. I mean, I worry when there's a reason to, like anyone else. But... I don't just sit around worrying about nothing. It's more about... just trying to keep up with what I'm supposed to be doing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a long-standing attention/regulation disorder characterized by persistent difficulty sustaining focus on mentally demanding tasks, procrastination/avoidance, forgetfulness, losing materials, and failure to follow through across multiple settings since childhood. Functional impact is present at work and in social/organizational responsibilities. Generalized excessive worry was denied, making an anxiety-based explanation less likely.
